title: MBTI vs Enneagram vs DISC vs Big Five for AI (Matcher)
description: Compare MBTI, Enneagram, DISC, Big Five (OCEAN), and Attachment for tuning AI assistants—plus an interactive 20-second matcher by workflow friction.
h1: Which personality system should you use to tune your AI?
dek: MBTI, Enneagram, DISC, Big Five (OCEAN), and Attachment control different layers of AI behavior—pick the exact template family in 20 seconds.
lede: AgentTune hosts 43 MIT-licensed tuning templates across five personality systems, plus five free self-report questionnaires. You do not need to take all five tests—or even any test—to pick a strong system prompt. Each framework excels at solving a different AI communication problem, from cutting preamble (MBTI / DISC) to calibrating bluntness and reassurance (Enneagram / Attachment) or adjusting one dimension cleanly (Big Five OCEAN).
answer: Pick DISC or MBTI when you want sharper structure and faster bottom-line delivery; pick Big Five (OCEAN) when you want a single trait lever (such as High Openness or Low Extraversion) without a full persona archetype; pick Enneagram or Attachment when your main friction is how candidly the assistant pushes back or cushions critical feedback.

sections.h2: What our September 2026 benchmark data says about choosing between systems.
sections.html:
• Models share tight default habits regardless of framework: Across 2,000 fresh September 2026 sessions covering GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1, Big Five Agreeableness clustered from 44.99 to 47.07 / 50 while DISC Dominance sat at a floor of 4.00 to 5.42 / 20. That explains why out-of-the-box defaults almost never feel sharp until you override them with behavioral rules.
  • Watch out for artificial tie-breaking in binary type quizzes: On OEJTS MBTI, 59 of 400 fresh sessions tied on at least one axis; silent < tie-breaking inflated apparent INTJ rates from 280/400 (70.0%) to 335/400 (83.8%). AgentTune’s interactive tests report exact ties rather than guessing a letter.
  • Instructions move the needle far more than framework labels: Our 60-reply controlled pilot raised answer-first openings from 14/20 to 19/20 and cut hedges per reply from 0.35 to 0.05 using concrete behavioral rules. Pick whichever system vocabulary makes those behavioral tradeoffs clearest for you—or skip personality tests altogether in the Communication Preferences Builder.

sections.h2: How to combine two frameworks without writing contradictory instructions.
sections.html:
If you like aspects of two frameworks—for example, DISC D for brevity plus Enneagram Type 8 or Big Five High Openness for pushback—do not paste two full 80-line templates into the same settings box. Instead:

  1. Choose one structural driver (DISC, MBTI, or OCEAN) to control answer order, length, and formatting.
  2. Borrow only 2–3 targeted rules for critique or tone from Enneagram or Attachment.
  3. Paste your combined draft into the Instruction Checker to catch accidental contradictions (“always concise” vs “explain everything in detail”), then run two quick before/after prompts in the Test Bench.

faq.q: Which personality system is most scientifically validated for communication preferences?
faq.a: Among the five public instruments here, the Big Five (measured via IPIP-50) has the strongest consensus support in personality psychology as continuous trait dimensions rather than discrete categories, making it ideal when you want to tune one habit at a time.

faq.q: Do I have to take a personality test to generate AgentTune custom instructions?
faq.a: No. Use the 20-second friction matcher above, browse the 43-file library directly by communication trait, or use the test-free Communication Preferences Builder.

faq.q: What is the fastest test if I want an AI tuning file in three minutes?
faq.a: Our free 16-item DISC assessment (ODAT) takes roughly three minutes in your browser with no email required, and gives you an instant primary style, optional blend, and paste-ready AI rules.

faq.q: Should I tell ChatGPT or Claude 'act as an INTJ' instead of pasting a full template?
faq.a: No. Bare four-letter labels push models toward caricatures or clichés. Concrete behavioral rules (putting conclusions first, omitting filler praise, naming unverified assumptions) work reliably across models.
